intro.title: Unnecessary Re-renders
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple counter app that demonstrates how React components can re-render unnecessarily, even when their props or state haven't changed. You'll learn about React's rendering behavior and how to identify wasteful re-renders using the React Developer Tools. The core concept involves understanding when and why components re-render, and how to optimize performance by preventing unnecessary updates. You'll work with functional components, state management using useState, and props in TypeScript to create a clear example of this common React performance issue.
intro.usecase: Unnecessary re-renders frequently occur in complex React applications like e-commerce dashboards where multiple components display real-time data. For example, when a user updates a product filter, only the product list should re-render—not the entire dashboard including user profile panels and shopping cart summaries. This pattern appears in interactive forms where typing in one field shouldn't cause validation messages in unrelated sections to flicker. Understanding and preventing unnecessary re-renders is crucial for maintaining smooth performance in data-intensive applications like analytics platforms and collaborative editing tools.
